sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Maritime Seafarer Staffing and Vessel Crew Management Agency

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Panama (unitary national jurisdiction; single registry and single taxation model; no sub-fiscal distinctions for corporate law)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil law system (Spanish-continental codification) with corporate-law heritage drawn from the Delaware General Corporation Law (Ley 32 de 1927) and a modernized commercial maritime code administered by the Panama Maritime Authority (Autoridad Marítima de Panamá - AMP).
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: United States–Panama Trade Promotion Agreement (in force 2012)
Central America–European Union Association Agreement (Panama trade and services pillar)
Double taxation and maritime convention between Panama and the United States on income from shipping and air transport (reciprocal exemption regime)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 23 de 27 de abril de 2015 (AML/CFT) as amended by Ley 70 de 2019 (creates the Registro de Beneficiario Final) and Ley 129 de 2020; Executive Decree 363 of 23 December 2022 (UBO Registry operative regulation); Decreto Ley 9 de 2020 (creation of the Superintendencia de Sujetos No Financieros - SSNF); Ley 32 de 1927 of Sociedades Anónimas; Banco Nacional tariff and UAF Resolution 1-2017 list screening instructions for obliged non-financial subjects.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (registry data accessible to the SSNF, UAF, tax authorities and obliged subjects exclusively for AML/CFT due diligence; not a fully public register; private client-nominee arrangements remain lawful but the nominee must disclose the beneficial owner to the obliged subject).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Poder de Representación (Power of Attorney) granted to the Panamanian incorporation attorney/registered agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Panamanian Notary Public or notary in the principal's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Panama acceded to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention; in force since 30 May 1991); consular legalization only where the origin state is not a Convention party

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing / certificate of existence of each corporate subscriber (where the incorporator is a foreign company)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or chamber of commerce of the foreign state
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the competent authority of the state of issue

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copies of each individual subscriber, director and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or certified notarial copy incorporated into the Panamanian Escritura Pública)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn Spanish translation of any foreign-language constitutive or shareholding documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: No separate legalization; notarized and protocolized within the Escritura Pública before the Panamanian notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Evidence of prior maritime manning license or crew-recruitment authorization of the foreign parent or ultimate beneficial owner (if a regulated crewing operator)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Maritime administration / flag state authority of the source country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization in the absence of apostille coverage

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Obliged subjects must perform risk-based client due diligence under Ley 23/2015 and comply with CFATF/FATF Recommendation 24: identify UBOs at the 10% statutory threshold; monitor PEPs (political, domestic and international-organisation) with source-of-funds verification; run continuous negative screening against the UN Consolidated Sanctions List, OFAC SDN/ SSI lists, the Panamanian UAF domestic counter-list, and EU/UK sanctions where payment rails require; suspicious transactions must be reported via the UAF's SIEC system; maritime crew-manning is classified Low_Risk_Standard for AML, subject to periodic compliance reviews by the SSNF.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá (RPP) electronic portal – 'Sistema de Trámites en Línea' at https://www.registro-publico.gob.pa and the one-stop enterprise window 'Panamá Emprende' (https://www.panamaemprende.gob.pa) for name reservation and S.A. creation.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Spanish is the official protocol language; corporate names may use Latin-script characters, numerals, proper names and words of any modern language provided they are transliterated into Latin letters; the corporate object clause must always be stated in Spanish in the Escritura; the index system records the name in Latin transliteration; abbreviations such as S.A., Ltd., Inc. are acceptable as long as the name remains distinguished in the RPP index.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banco / Banca / Banking (prior authorization from the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá)
Seguros / Reaseguros / Insurance (prior authorization from the Superintendencia de Seguros y Reaseguros)
Valores / Bolsa / Fondo de Inversión / Exchange (prior authorization from the Superintendencia del Mercado de Valores)
Fiduciario / Trust / Fideicomiso (prior authorization from the SSNF or Superintendencia de Bancos)
Nacional / Estatal / Oficial / Gobierno / Ministerio (misleading state-implication prohibitions)
Panamá / Panama (restricted where name may confuse with state entities or registered state marks)
References to casino, gaming, pharmacy, health and defence activities requiring other ministerial clearances
Any name identical, spelt with minor arithmetical letters, or phonetically equivalent to an existing registered company
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: When the RPP name-approval unit denies or observes the proposed name, the applicant may: (i) present a Recurso de Reconsideración before the RPP Directorate within 5 useful days of notification; (ii) appeal to the superior hierarchical authority (Recurso de Apelación) in accordance with Ley 38 de 2000; (iii) in parallel, request a new search and submit up to 3 alternative names through Panamá Emprende. Rejected names are released immediately; a fresh search certificate with a new fee is required for each alternative.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Partially permissive. The S.A. may register at the office address of its licensed resident agent and no physical office is required for the pure holding/administrative shell; however, for the future DGMM crew recruitment license of the Panama Maritime Authority and for multi-currency payroll substance, an operational presence (physical office or supervised alternate premises in Panama with a qualified manning manager) will be required; virtual-office-only substance is insufficient for active maritime agency licensing.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Stage-1 registry phase: below 5% (random monitoring by RPP and UAF red-flag triggers); licensing phase under AMP/DGMM annual compliance inspections: 30-40% probability of unannounced physical verification for crew-agency licensees; entity must keep minute books, payroll records and UBO filings at the registered agent's office for inspection readiness.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name search and certificate of non-registration (Certificado de Búsqueda y No Registro)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official tariff for certified search certificate (B/35.00 standard; B/11.00 when filed via Panamá Emprende web service)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial preparation and execution of the Escritura Pública (incorporation deed) including protocolized Spanish statements
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarial tariff of the Colegio de Notarios de Panamá (average fixed notary fee range B/100-B/150 for standard S.A.)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration of the incorporation deed in the Mercantile Section of the Registro Público (folios and inscription fees)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Inscription rights calculated on the number of deed pages and folio charges (typical total B/220-B/320)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Initial franchise rights apportionment and national stamp duties on the articles (impuesto de timbre / registro de aviso)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministry of Economy and Finance
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Stamp tax tariff of 0.50%-1.0% on the nominal capital portion combined with fixed municipal aviso charges

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague apostille of foreign shareholder documents and authorization deeds (per document, 4-document bundle)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent apostille authority in the country of origin (e.g., U.S. Secretary of State offices, FCDO in UK)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official apostille fees of the origin state (B/20-B/60 per document; total bundle estimated B/200-B/280)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified Spanish translation of foreign-language corporate documents (per source page, typical set)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of B/25- B/50 per standard page for constitutional documents (flat set B/120-B/180)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Year-one resident agent service (Agente Residente) including registered-office address, statutory record keeping and Government correspondence relay
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Panamanian resident agent (law firm or registered agent company)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark B/300-B/600 per year for standard S.A.; higher for regulated maritime operators

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 32 de 1927 (Commercial Companies Act of Panama), as amended by Ley 2 de 2015 and complementary maritime statutes; Articles 1, 10, 24 and 45 govern formation, minimum capital, filing and share issuance for a Sociedad Anónima (S.A.).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección Mercantil (Mercantile Registry Section of the National Public Registry of Panama)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública (notarial public deed) containing the Pacto Social and Estatutos, registered with the Sección Mercantil of the Registro Público de Panamá
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Statutory minimum capital is USD 10,000 represented by 10,000 ordinary shares of USD 1.00 each. The capital need not be deposited or escrowed at incorporation; shares may be issued as partially paid, subject to a board call for instalments. No mandatory paid-up capital certificate is required by Ley 32 de 1927.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: First Board Resolution: On 15 May 2025, the first board of directors of the Sociedad Anónima unanimously resolved: 1. Share Capital: approve the statutory capital of USD 10,000, allocate the subscribed shares to the founding shareholders and record them as fully or partially paid as determined by this board. 2. Registered Office: adopt the registered office address in Panama City, Republic of Panama, and designate the corresponding physical business address for maritime regulator filings. 3. Officers: appoint the President, Secretary and Treasurer, authorizing them to execute corporate documents and banking instruments. 4. Delegation: authorize the resident agent to file all statutory forms. Certified by the Secretary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Pre-Approval and Agent Appointment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – SIRI online registration system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request through SIRI and obtain the Certificado de Nominación confirming the availability of the preferred corporate name. The name is held for 30 business days. Simultaneously execute the registered agent agreement and prepare the power of attorney for the notarial phase.
required_dossiers: Draft corporate name and two alternates
Passport or national ID copies of founding shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the requested name is rejected, file a new nomination through SIRI with a distinctive suffix; administrative reconsideration is available where the refusal is based on confusing similarity.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Public Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public (Notaría) in Panama, acting before the Registro Público
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Deliver the name certificate, draft Pacto Social and Estatutos, and shareholder identity documents to the chosen notary. The shareholders sign the Escritura Pública before the notary; the notary authenticates the execution and issues certified copies for subsequent registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary issues observations, amend the deed and re-execute before the same or a replacement notary; corrections are incorporated by marginal note before presentation to the Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Mandatory Commercial Registration with the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección Mercantil
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the original Escritura Pública together with certified copies and proof of payment of registry fees. The Registrar examines legal validity and issues the Ficha Registral and certification of legal existence of the Sociedad Anónima.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the public deed
Application for insolvency and juridical person certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry returns queries, effect corrections via the notary and refile; administrative appeal is available if registration is denied after correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration (RUC) and Aviso de Operación
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the tax registration form through the DGI online tax portal, attaching the certified incorporation deed and address evidence. Obtain the RUC certificate and generate the Aviso de Operación which is the tax identification basis for all subsequent municipal and maritime licences.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the registered public deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DGI rejects or suspends registration due to name or address inconsistency, correct the third-party data through the DGI service window and resubmit; overdue penalties are settled before final issuance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Operating Licence and Company Tax Enrolment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alcaldía de Panamá – Fondo de Inversión Municipal, Tax Administration Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the RUC certificate, certified corporate documents and the office lease or title to the Municipal Treasury. Pay the annual patent fee and obtain the Patente Municipal and Aviso de Operación municipal, which are preconditions for employer registration and the AMP maritime crew agency licence.
required_dossiers: Municipal tax form and fee receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Municipality rejects due to land-use or address mismatch, obtain a zoning compatibility certificate or correct the physical address data at the municipal window and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Employer Registration with CSS and Labour Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Caja de Seguro Social (CSS) – Employer Registration Office, Digital Services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company as an employer through the CSS employer portal using the Ficha Registral, RUC and legal representative credentials. Obtain the employer registration number required for payroll deductions and submit the corresponding employer notification to MITRADEL for labour statistics.
required_dossiers: Ficha Registral or certified corporate certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registration is blocked by name or employer-ID mismatch, confirm the RUC status with the DGI, correct the corporate data at CSS and resubmit within the compliance window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Seafarer Recruitment and Placement Agency Licence
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de la Gente de Mar, Autoridad Marítima de Panamá (AMP)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the standardized application for the Seafarer Recruitment and Placement Agency Licence to the AMP maritime single window, including the incorporation certificate, municipal patent, office premises documentation, crew management staff qualifications, police clearance and the MLC 2006 compliance undertaking. AMP carries out an on-site inspection and, once satisfied, registers the agency and issues the licence for operation.
required_dossiers: Ficha Registral and certificado de personería
Office floor plan and fire safety layout
Qualifications and resumes of crewing administrators
MLC 2006 compliance and service commitment letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If AMP raises supplementary observations, complete the additional dossier within the stated period and resubmit; a denial may be appealed through the hierarchical administrative route before the Minister or the AMP Board.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Dirección General de la Gente de Mar, Autoridad Marítima de Panamá (AMP)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licencia para Agencia de Reclutamiento y Colocación de Gente de Mar (Seafarer Recruitment and Placement Agency Licence)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) – Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category I (Exempt from full EIA registration) for purely administrative office activity under Decreto Ejecutivo 57 de 1997 and Resolución 123 de 2014. If the crew agency facility includes seafarer training workshops, fuel storage or port-adjacent workshops, it is upgraded to Category II requiring a preliminary environmental study.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater: office effluent is discharged to the municipal sewer and permitted by MiAMBIENTE; septic systems, if applicable, must meet BOD5 below 10 mg/L. No VOC or significant air emissions for the crewing office. Solid waste is segregated, stored and disposed in accordance with Decreto Ejecutivo 6 de 2021.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire prevention certificate issued by the Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá, structural load and occupancy inspection by a licensed engineer, and occupational health clearance by MITRADEL – Dirección General de Salud Ocupacional. The office must maintain an approved fire safety plan, fire extinguishers, emergency exits and workplace ergonomic compliance for crew-staffing operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF), Republic of Panama. Official online services portal: SII / e-Tax 7.0 accessible via https://sitio.dgi.gob.pa; public information website: www.dgi.gob.pa. Maritime-sector coordination is with the Panama Maritime Authority (AMP) for vessel-related registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Complete S.A. incorporation in the Public Registry (Pacto Social, notarized Escritura, resident agent appointment). 2. Assemble foreign-owner KYC: apostilled passport copies, Spanish translations, and beneficial-ownership declaration. 3. File the Aviso de Operación (Notice of Operation) with the DGI registration questionnaire through the SII/e-Tax portal (or via notary or licensed CPA) specifying the ISIC 5222 crew recruitment activity, estimated annual gross income, and Panamanian correspondence address. 4. Receive the Registro Único de Contribuyente (RUC/NIT) and activate the taxpayer's digital signature certificate. 5. If physically operating: obtain the municipal Aviso de Operación (Municipio de Panamá), register as a CSS employer for payroll, and inscribe locally hired crew/administrative staff in the educational insurance regime. 6. Purely offshore crew-managing S.A.s must still keep the RUC active, pay the annual franchise tax (Taxo Único), and file territorial-source income tax returns; foreign-owned entities must have a resident agent and a licensed Contador Público Autorizado co-sign tax filings.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not provide US-style check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch elections; classification follows the statutory territorial source rule. Available structuring elections include: (a) SEM / Multinational Headquarters election under Law 41/2007 to treat regional crew-management back-office income as exempt from ISR and ITBMS; (b) an election, recognized by the Panama Maritime Authority under Law 56/1996, to be classified as a maritime auxiliary services provider, confirming that international crew-supply fees are not Panamanian-source income; and (c) a pre-filing source-of-income ruling (Consulta) with the DGI to segregate Panamanian domestic manning services from offshore crew-placement fees. There is no pass-through election; the S.A. is irrevocably subject to entity-level territorial taxation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS – Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (goods-and-services transfer tax; Law 15 of 2017 as amended, Código Fiscal Arts. 1057–1159)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: B/.36,000 per annum under Law 15/2017 and its implementing regulations; Balboa is at 1:1 par with the US Dollar. Taxpayers with annual gross taxable sales/income above B/.36,000 must register for ITBMS; registration is compulsory from business commencement for importers and digital-service providers irrespective of the threshold. Businesses below the threshold may opt into the simplified small-taxpayer regime without input VAT credit.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory DGI electronic invoicing: all ITBMS-registered businesses must issue invoices as XML through the DGI e-Tax 7.0/SII portal or an authorized PSFE (Proveedor de Servicios de Facturación Electrónica). Each invoice must be transmitted to the DGI in real time and obtain a 'Código de Rastreo' plus a validatable fiscal QR before delivery; paper invoice formats were phased out during the 2020–2023 compulsory rollout. The DGI automatically validates RUC status, activity class (ISIC 5222), and tax-treatment code; zero-rated export invoices must reference the underlying export evidence. Absence of integrated e-invoicing triggers automatic disallowance of input VAT credits and automatic monthly ITBMS assessments.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: ITBMS zero-rating (Art. 64, Law 15/2017) is claimable for exports of goods and for services rendered in Panama but effectively exported, i.e., economically used or consumed outside Panama by a non-resident party. A crew recruitment agency may zero-rate manning and crew-management commissions if: (i) the contractual counterparty is a non-resident shipowner or operator without a Panamanian taxable establishment; (ii) seafarers are deployed on foreign-flag or internationally trading vessels; (iii) the DGI e-invoice designates the supply as 'exportación de servicios'; and (iv) the agency retains the signed service contract, vessel registration certificate, crew employment agreements, and bank SWIFT/remittance evidence proving foreign payment. Domestic manning of Panamanian coastal vessels remains taxable at 7% ITBMS and must be segregated in accounting; combined export/domestic billing without separate documentation risks a full-turnover reassessment.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación filed through Panama's ASYCUDA/SIEC customs clearance system) for any physical goods or vessel stores
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or International Carrier's Certificate evidencing foreign destination or international voyage
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT credit advice evidencing collection of the export proceeds
Non-resident shipowner/operator identification (corporate extract, IMO company code, foreign tax registration)
Signed Crew Manning Service Contract specifying commission/fee calculation and place of performance
Foreign or Panama Ship Registration Certificate and crew articles confirming international-trade deployment
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI audit programs specifically target maritime service exporters. Unsupported zero-rating is reclassified as taxable at 7% on the gross invoice amount, with monthly mora interest at 1% and a 10% recargo on the unpaid tax (Arts. 756–761 Código Fiscal), plus fines that can reach 200% of the evaded tax under Arts. 748–756 Código Fiscal. Fabricated bills of lading, false non-resident certificates, or ante-dated remittance evidence trigger criminal liability for 'ilícito tributario' under Art. 55 of Law 15/2017 (2–6 years imprisonment), cancellation of the RUC, and joint and several liability of the resident agent and directors for proven fraud. DGI clawback limitation is 5 years, extended to 10 years where no return was filed or fraud is demonstrated.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) as exclusive banking regulator; the Republic of Panama has no traditional central bank. Banco Nacional de Panamá performs fiscal agency functions for the State and facilitates payment clearing.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama is a fully dollarized economy; the US Dollar is legal tender, and the Panamanian balboa exists only as coinage at par with the USD. Full convertibility is available for both capital and current account operations, with no exchange controls, no authorization requirements for dividend remittances, and no restrictions on profit repatriation. Corporate profits are freely transferable abroad after compliance with Panamanian source-income taxation and treaty reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender or mandatory conversion rules apply. Panama does not require exporters to repatriate, convert, or hold export proceeds in any designated currency or account.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low to Medium feasibility. Panama's Digital Hub Law (Law 166 of 2020) provides a regulated licensing framework for FinTech and electronic payment companies, but offshore digital EMIs are not permitted to service Panamanian entities without a local license, physical presence, and SBP compliance. Unlicensed offshore EMIs pose concentration and AML risks and cannot serve as the principal treasury rail for crew payroll settlement.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Tier-1 Panamanian banks generally require a face-to-face KYC interview with at least one director and the ultimate beneficial owner at the time of corporate account opening. Remote opening is occasionally permitted on a case-by-case basis for non-resident corporations using apostilled powers of attorney, notarized board resolutions, and certified passport copies, but a resident legal representative or a member of the board is typically required to be physically present for enhanced due diligence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume, multi-currency payroll disbursements to foreign seafarers and vessel crew
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Statutory crew manning agreements, ISPS/MLC 2006 compliance records, crew lists, individual seafarer employment contracts, payroll ledger, remittance beneficiary schedules, OFAC/SBP sanctions screening results, and documented source of funds from vessel owners and ship management principals.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity in ultimate beneficial ownership through a Panamanian Private Interest Foundation or bearer-share legacy structures
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Foundation deed and bylaws, notarized appointment of the council, protector declaration, current UBO register under the Panamanian financial transparency law, apostilled incorporation documents, legal opinion from a licensed Panamanian attorney, and independent confirmation of source of wealth.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transactions referencing high-risk maritime jurisdictions or port states subject to FATF monitoring
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Vessel ownership registry documents, flag state certificates, port-call documentation, Taliban-era and international sanctions screening output, charter party evidence, end-use and end-user declarations, and a written narrative of the commercial transportation route.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity injections and shareholder loans are routed via SWIFT MT103 over CHIPS/Fedwire correspondent networks to the company's US-dollar operational account in Panama. The SWIFT purpose field must clearly state 'Share Capital Contribution' or 'Intra-Group Loan' accompanied by a board resolution, an updated corporate register showing share issuance, and a copy of the instruction from the remitting bank. For due diligence, the beneficiary bank will request a legal counsel opinion confirming the subscription price and the absence of money laundering indicators.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlement payments to suppliers and crew wages use high-value SWIFT MT103 messages through locally licensed clearing participants. For procurement of provisions, fuel, and vessel supplies, commercial letters of credit (LC at sight or deferred) are established at the operational bank for beneficiary risk mitigation. Frequent moderate-value payroll disbursements can be aggregated and processed via batch SWIFT payments with remote approval controls under the payroll service agreement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX Forwards executed via international bank desks and advised by the Panamanian operating bank for EUR, GBP, PHP, and other crew pay currencies
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) where local currency pairs are illiquid or restricted in key remittance corridors
Cross-Currency Swaps for long-term payroll obligations in Asian and European currencies
FX Options sold by regulated global markets counterparties to cap severe volatility in emerging market crew-sourcing jurisdictions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Franchise Tax — Tasa Única Anual (base bracket for total assets up to USD 150,000; graduated scale above that under Law 129 of 2021, Fiscal Code Article 892)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) — Ministry of Economy and Finance, via TUNA Digital Platform
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 15 July (DGI administrative due date in recent fiscal years; statutory accrual window is the first calendar quarter, originally 15 March)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% late-payment surcharge plus statutory monthly interest (approximately 1% per month); failure to pay for three consecutive years authorizes the Public Registry to strike off the company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return — Declaración Jurada de Renta (Formulario 1)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) — TUNA Digital Platform
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 15 March following the close of the 31 December fiscal year; extended filing window applies to taxpayers required to attach audited financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% recargo on the tax due for late filing/payment plus statutory interest at 10% per annum; non-filing fines up to USD 1,000; fraud penalties from 50% to 200% of omitted tax; denial of 'paz y salvo' tax clearance certificates.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Final Beneficiary (UBO) Declaration — Declaración Anual de Beneficiarios Finales under Law 254 of 2021 and Executive Decree 238 of 2021
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGI — Registro de Beneficiarios Finales, via TUNA Digital Platform
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March following the reporting fiscal year; share transfers occurring during the year must be declared within 30 days from execution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to USD 50,000 for non-compliance under Law 254 of 2021; continued default may accrue daily penalties and the annual franchise tax payment may be gated on completion of the UBO filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Renewal of Private Maritime Recruitment and Placement Agency License (ship crew manning agency) — includes update of crewing placement statistics and evidence of MLC 2006 compliance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Panama Maritime Authority (AMP) — Dirección General de Gente de Mar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before the license expiry date (anniversary of original grant); renewal application must be submitted before expiry to avoid interruption
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: License suspension and cease-and-desist of all crewing recruitment and placement operations; administrative fines under AMP maritime labour regulations; persistent non-renewal results in license revocation and loss of manning-agent status.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit where annual gross income exceeds USD 3,000,000 in the preceding fiscal year (DGI requirement to attach audited financial statements to the annual income tax return); also mandatory for issuers of securities registered with the Superintendencia del Mercado de Valores, regulated financial entities, and companies for which the AMP requires audited financial statements as evidence of financial solvency at license renewal.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the IASB for public-interest entities; IFRS for SMEs permitted for other companies; financial statements normally presented in USD; accounting records must be available in Spanish or accompanied by a Spanish translation for DGI inspection.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each calendar year, every Panama legal entity must file or reconfirm its final beneficiary schedule through the DGI's TUNA portal under Law 254 of 2021 and Executive Decree 238 of 2021. The annual confirmation must reflect share transfers and control changes during the reporting year; share transfers executed during the year must additionally be declared within 30 days from execution; completion of the UBO filing is a practical precondition for payment of the annual franchise tax.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro de Registro de Accionistas)
Register of Directors (Libro de Registro de Directores)
Minute Book (Libro de Actas — Board and Shareholders)
Share Transfer Ledger (Libro de Registro de Transferencias de Acciones)
Final Beneficiaries Records retained per Law 254 of 2021

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 – 25,000 per audit engagement depending on agency size and transaction volume

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday for a standard Panama S.A. Territorial taxation applies: only Panama-source income is subject to CIT; foreign-source income is exempt. No preferential deduction is available to a ship-crew recruitment agency under the SEM or Panama Pacifico special regimes unless specifically licensed therein.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form DGI-22 'Informe de Renta' (Annual Income Tax Return), filed electronically through the DGI e-Tax 2.0 portal (https://www.dgitax.com).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (standard fiscal year: January 1 – December 31; alternative fiscal years require prior DGI authorization).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after the fiscal year-end. For a calendar-year corporation, the filing and payment deadline is March 31 of the following year; no automatic filing extension exists.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Ingresos gravables de fuente panameña (taxable Panama-source gross revenue, including crew placement commissions and vessel crew management fees sourced in Panama).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only revenue whose 'causa panameña' is established by services performed or management exercised in Panama; exclude revenue attributable to a foreign branch or foreign crew supply operations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Ingresos exentos y de fuente extranjera (exempt and foreign-source revenue).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: List commissions and management fees derived from contracts centered outside Panama, provided that no Panamanian establishment performs the services and no source activity occurs in Panama.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Costos y gastos deducibles (deductible costs and expenses, net of non-deductible provisions).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct only expenses economically linked to Panama-source revenue; invoice and payroll documentation must be kept in Spanish or English and retained for six years.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Depreciación y amortización del período (annual depreciation and amortization).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply statutory rates to local fixed assets; foreign-asset depreciation is not allocable to Panama-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Renta neta del período (net income before NOL utilization).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Calculate only Panamanian tax-basis profit; do not include foreign sources unless subject to tax in Panama by treaty rule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Pérdidas compensables de años anteriores (NOL carryforward utilized).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use only losses from Panama-source operations, limited to the five-year carryforward period; treaty or attribution rules may not extend this.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Renta neta gravable (taxable net income after NOL).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This is the base subjected to the 25% rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Impuesto sobre la renta determinado (CIT determined at 25%).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply 25% to Box 7; foreign tax credits are not available under Panama's territorial system.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Pagos a cuenta, retenciones y créditos (advance payments, withholding credits and treaty credits).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include local MNG payments (monthly advance payments) and any treaty-reduced withholding credits evidenced by appropriate TRC certificates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Saldo por pagar o saldo a favor (final liability or refund).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Remit the balance in USD/Balboa via approved national bank channels; overpayments may be refunded only after DGI administrative review.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Anexo de Precios de Transferencia (transfer pricing declaration annexed to Form DGI-22).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Required when the crewing agency undertakes controlled transactions with foreign related shipowners or affiliated payroll entities; failing the annex invalidates the return for audit purposes.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: surcharge of 10% of the tax payable and a minimum B/. 50 fine when no tax is due. Late payment: monthly interest of 1% on the unpaid amount. Incomplete annexes or refusal to submit books trigger fines from B/. 100 to B/. 5,000, and the DGI may deny the tax clearance 'Paz y Salvo' required for vessel contracting and license renewal.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% (final) on dividends distributed to non-resident shareholders; 5% for resident shareholders. Where paid profits had not been subjected to 25% corporate tax, the distributing company must first pay a 10% complementary tax (impuesto complementario) at the corporate level.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim a reduced DTA rate: (1) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the shareholder's home tax authority, dated within the last six months; (2) submit the TRC with a beneficial ownership declaration to the Panamanian payer before the dividend is paid; (3) the payer retains the documentation for six years and reflects the treaty rate in Box 9 of Form DGI-22; (4) the shareholder must satisfy any limitation-on-benefits clause in the applicable treaty. Panama's treaty network is limited; relief is available only where the specific DTA is ratified and in force (e.g., France, Netherlands, UK, UAE, Mexico, South Korea).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory interest withholding on non-resident lenders: 2.5% effective (10% deemed net income × 25%). Statutory royalties and technical services (including maritime management know-how and software licensing): 12.5% effective (50% deemed net × 25%). Treaty rates, where applicable, commonly reduce interest to 0–5% and royalties to 5–10%, subject to beneficial ownership and anti-abuse rules.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: B/. 3,000,000 (three million Panamanian balboas, equivalent to USD 3,000,000) in gross annual revenue or in cross-border related-party transactions triggers the obligation to prepare and submit the Local File and Master File. An annual transfer pricing annex (Anexo de Partes Relacionadas) is required for controlled transactions exceeding B/. 250,000 in the fiscal year.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama does not administer a UAE-style ESR code. However, Article 766 of the Fiscal Code and AML Law 23 of 2011 require real office premises, local employees, payroll records and board-management substance in Panama to support Panama-source treatment, DTA claims and the validity of the corporate seat. For a crew recruitment agency, the statutory maritime crewing license, local crew consultants and payroll ledgers constitute the core evidence of substance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Underreporting crew-placement commissions, fabricating payroll entries, using invoice mills to inflate deductible costs, or shifting Panama-source income to a foreign shell without business purpose.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment of 2 to 5 years and fines equal to 100% to 300% of the tax evaded; mandatory inclusion on the DGI public defaulters' register; suspension of the taxpayer's RUC (tax identification number) and cancellation of maritime crewing licenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and managers who sign false returns face criminal prosecution as co-authors; personal assets may be seized under the DGI tax lien; travel bans may be imposed by the migration authorities; director disqualification of up to five years can be ordered.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Absence of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the Panamanian S.A. with only a registered-agent address, no local employees, no physical office, and no board or contract files, while recording substantial crew payroll and commissions through Panama.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI recharacterization of all profits as Panama-source if management is factually exercised from Panama; denial of treaty relief; fines under Law 23 of 2011 of up to USD 1,000,000 for related financial institutions; administrative deregistration by the Public Registry after prolonged annual fee non-compliance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts may pierce the corporate veil under Panama's fraudulent-veil doctrine; directors become personally liable for unpaid corporate taxes and crew wages; immigration and customs watchlists may block exit from Panama; criminal asset forfeiture extends to personal properties used in the scheme.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging foreign affiliated shipowners sub-market commissions, paying excessive management fees to sister entities, or failing to file the required annual TP annex and Local/Master File when thresholds are met.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI adjustment to arm's-length income; fine equal to 10% of the aggregate value of undocumented related-party transactions; monthly interest and surcharges on the underpaid CIT; possible reclassification of the excess as a deemed dividend subject to 10% withholding.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve non-arm's-length contracts may be jointly and severally liable for the tax deficiency where the company is undercapitalized or insolvent; signing officers face criminal liability for submitting false TP certifications.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering and Beneficial Ownership (Law 23 of 2011)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Serving foreign shipowners without registering Ultimate Beneficial Owners, accepting cash-backed payroll kickbacks from seafarers, or allowing the corporate account to be used for third-party fund flows without AML due-diligence controls.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines from USD 10,000 to USD 1,000,000 per violation; suspension or revocation of the crewing license issued by the Dirección General de Marina Mercante; criminal prosecution for money laundering under Panama Criminal Code Article 254 with imprisonment of 5 to 12 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Board members and the designated compliance officer can be indicted for money laundering; personal and corporate accounts are subject to freezing and forfeiture; exit bans are routinely imposed during the criminal investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to File, Registry Delinquency and Record-Keeping Breach
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Omitting the annual income tax return in a zero-activity year, failing to pay the S.A. annual Public Registry fee (Annuity), or destroying books and contract files before the six-year statutory retention period expires.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Late-filing surcharge of 10% plus 1% monthly interest; Public Registry delinquency penalties of USD 300 per year plus surcharges; RUC suspension blocks bank account operation, maritime license renewal and vessel-crew contracting; failure to keep records triggers fines of up to B/. 5,000 and DGI's right to issue a deemed assessment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: After deregistration, directors become personally liable for obligations contracted while the company lacked legal standing; a DGI travel ban may be issued for unfiled tax debts; resident agents may file criminal complaints if directors mislead compliance.
